title: A Blow‑by‑Blow Account of What Would Happen If the Yellowstone Supervolcano Erupted Now - Nautilus
gist: A worst-case thought experiment by disaster and volcano experts (Kelman and Blackett, via The Conversation) of a Yellowstone VEI 8 super-eruption: months of escalating warning signs, evacuation of ~200,000, ash disabling power grids and supply chains, a North American agricultural collapse driving global food prices, banking/insurance crises and a global recession, ~1.5°C cooling, and 0.7-1.3 billion premature deaths over a decade—yet not the end of humanity.

insights.claim: Yellowstone is monitored continuously by seismometers, GPS stations, strainmeters, geyser sensors, satellites, gas sampling and field surveys, so a super-eruption would likely be preceded by weeks to months of detectable unrest.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Tail-risk catastrophe would not be a pure surprise; there would be a window for positioning.

insights.claim: No single signal (an earthquake swarm, ground deformation, temperature or gas change) implies an eruption; scientists worry when several such changes happen together.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: False-alarm-prone single indicators argue for waiting for confluence before acting on volcanic headlines.
insights.quote: Scientists are more concerned about several such changes happening together.

insights.claim: Yellowstone has produced alarming signal combinations before without eruption: in 2013-2014 parts of the caldera rose over 15 cm a year, culminating in a magnitude 4.8 quake (the largest since 1975), later attributed to hydrothermal fluids rather than magma.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Historical false positives mean market reactions to Yellowstone unrest are likely overreactions early on.
insights.quote: Between 2013 and 2014, parts of the caldera began rising at rates of more than 15 centimetres a year and earthquake activity increased.

insights.claim: In the scenario, eruption probability within three months rises from 6-9% to 21-27% at the 'advisory' stage, and then to 85-92% within three weeks when the alert is raised to 'watch'.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Illustrates how a catastrophe-risk probability path could evolve, relevant to cat-bond and insurance pricing.
insights.quote: The probability of it happening within three months increases from 6-9% to 21-27%.

insights.claim: Volcanologists avoid public disputes over uncertain interpretations, coordinating private debate and regular unified public updates to avoid damage from public controversy.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Official communications will be deliberately measured; information edge lies in raw monitoring data.
insights.quote: the volcanologists have learned how damaging it can be when volcanic uncertainties morph into a full-blown dispute, played out in public

insights.claim: Despite rising probabilities, politicians are expected to avoid specific declarations under uncertainty, while FEMA privately plans for a large-scale evacuation it may fear is hopeless in a worst case.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Policy response lags scientific signals, creating a gap between risk and official action.
insights.quote: Due to the uncertainties, the politicians make no specific declaration.

insights.claim: A 100 km evacuation zone around Yellowstone National Park would affect roughly 200,000 residents plus thousands of visitors.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Scale of direct displacement is manageable relative to the downstream economic effects.
insights.quote: An evacuation zone extending 100 kilometres beyond Yellowstone National Park is announced, affecting roughly 200,000 residents

insights.claim: Facing an imminent super-eruption, world leaders would choose between global cooperation and a repeat of COVID-19-style global shuttering, with the latter seen as more likely.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Expect border closures and hoarding rather than coordination in global catastrophes.
insights.quote: They must make a choice: help each other as a global village or repeat COVID-19 style global shuttering.

insights.claim: Many countries would likely refuse 'volcano refugees', while the wealthy with multiple passports self-evacuate and the poorest and most marginalised are left behind.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Disasters amplify inequality; second-passport and relocation demand rises with tail-risk awareness.
insights.quote: More likely, many countries could be reticent to accept “volcano refugees”

insights.claim: Imminent-disaster news would spawn both deniers and conspiracy theorists, including claims that the observatory is paid by foreign billionaires to bring down the US.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Disinformation would complicate evacuation compliance and market sentiment.

insights.claim: Underground bunkers are judged an overly optimistic protection against a super-eruption.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Doomsday-prep products overpromise against this class of tail risk.
insights.quote: who think their well-stocked underground bunkers will protect them (an overly optimistic belief)

insights.claim: The eruption would likely begin with phreatomagmatic explosions as magma vaporises hydrothermal water, which expands about 1,700 times when converted to steam at atmospheric pressure.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Explains the opening phase and why early casualties could be limited by exclusion zones.
insights.quote: At atmospheric pressure, water can expand in volume around 1,700 times when converted to steam.

insights.claim: The eruption column would rise 30-50 km, far above commercial aircraft cruising altitude of about 13 km, and be visible from Denver ~800 km away.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Aviation would be shut over much of North America.
insights.quote: creating a vast eruption column rising 30-50 kilometers into the atmosphere—far above commercial passenger aircraft

insights.claim: A VEI 8 super-eruption was last witnessed by humanity 74,000 years ago at Toba in Indonesia; Yellowstone's last super-eruption was about 631,000 years ago.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Base rates are extremely low, framing this as a deep tail risk.
insights.quote: It was 74,000 years ago that humanity last witnessed this scale of eruption with Toba in Indonesia.

insights.claim: Immediate deaths could be limited to up to about 1,000 thanks to exclusion zones, with further casualties from vehicle crashes, fires, heart and breathing problems, suicide, and generator-related electrocution and carbon monoxide poisoning.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: The human toll is driven far more by secondary systemic effects than the blast itself.
insights.quote: There may be up to 1,000 immediate human deaths, including people who refused to move.

insights.claim: Damp ash conducts electricity, short-circuiting power lines and substations, and also clogs machinery and generator intakes, causing grid failures across affected regions.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Grid vulnerability to ash is an underappreciated utility and insurance exposure.
insights.quote: Warnings had not been heeded that damp ash conducts electricity, short circuiting power lines and substations.

insights.claim: Power failure cascades into water pumps, sewage treatment, heating, fuel stations, mobile and internet networks, with supermarket shelves emptying nationwide as supply chains break down.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Electricity is the single point of failure for nearly all critical services.
insights.quote: As electricity fails, so do water pumps, sewage treatment, heating systems, fuel stations and mobile phone and internet networks.

insights.claim: Billings, Montana, would eventually receive more than a metre of ash (one model says up to 1.8 m), while Salt Lake City and Boise get tens of centimetres, and ash devastates farmland across at least eight states.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Regional real assets and agriculture in the Mountain West would be effectively written off.
insights.quote: one published model of a Yellowstone supereruption predicts the city as receiving up to 1.8 metres of ash

insights.claim: Airports across North America would repeatedly close for months whenever winds remobilise ash, keeping airspace unreliable.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Airlines and air freight would face prolonged, intermittent disruption rather than a single shock.
insights.quote: airports across North America repeatedly close whenever winds remobilise the ash

insights.claim: Some countries would airlift relief to the US but simultaneously worry about stockpiling for themselves.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Expect export restrictions and hoarding of food and essentials by other nations.
insights.quote: Some countries airlift or airdrop humanitarian relief supplies, but are also concerned about stockpiling for themselves.

insights.claim: Losses of American and Canadian grain, maize and soya exports would drive global food prices up.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Agricultural commodities would spike; food importers face inflation and instability.
insights.quote: The loss of American and Canadian grain, maize and soya exports drives global food prices upwards.

insights.claim: Unreliable airspace and transport, agricultural losses, business disruption and reconstruction costs would trigger banking and insurance crises and a global recession.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: A North American super-eruption is a systemic financial tail risk via insurers and banks, not just a regional event.
insights.quote: trigger banking and insurance crises, producing a global recession

insights.claim: Losses to agriculture, transport and insurance, plus refugee flows, could lead Canada, Mexico and most Caribbean and Central American countries to declare states of emergency.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Neighbouring economies tightly linked to the US would suffer spillover crises.

insights.claim: Stratospheric sulphate aerosols would cause a 'volcanic cooling episode' of likely no more than about 1.5°C global average, though regions and seasons could see much larger changes, with central North America staying far cooler.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Multi-year climate shock would hit northern-hemisphere crop yields and energy demand.
insights.quote: Modelling suggests it’s unlikely to cool the global average by more than about 1.5°C

insights.claim: Over ten years, societies would shift to a more agrarian lifestyle, converting recreational facilities to food production, expanding greenhouses, vertical farming, insect farming and seaweed farming as livestock declines.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Long-run demand would rotate toward food-security technologies and away from leisure.

insights.claim: Fishing would surge and deplete stocks until controls are enacted; where rules are not agreed or enforced, starvation and migration would be rampant.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Governance quality would determine which regions recover.
insights.quote: Where rules are not agreed or enforced, starvation and migration are rampant.

insights.claim: Before the eruption, about 4.4 billion of the world's 8.3 billion people lack full safe freshwater access; a decade later this could be 4.8 billion, with world population falling to 7.9 billion.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Highlights pre-existing global water insecurity as a baseline vulnerability.
insights.quote: Before the eruption, around 4.4 billion people from the world’s population of 8.3 billion lacked full, safe freshwater access.

insights.claim: Excess mortality analyses could suggest 0.7-1.3 billion premature deaths from the eruption and its impacts, yet it would not end humanity or come close.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Even the worst natural tail risk is survivable for civilisation, but with enormous human cost.
insights.quote: Excess mortality analyses could suggest 0.7-1.3 billion premature deaths due to the eruption and its impacts.

insights.claim: Collapsed health systems would turn survivable diagnoses lethal, and the eruption could provide long-term evidence that silica in ash raises silicosis, lung cancer and cardiovascular disease.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Health-system resilience, not the hazard itself, drives long-run mortality.
insights.quote: Survivable diagnoses become lethal.

insights.claim: When ash clears, sunlight returns and fears of human-caused warming revive, as heat stored in oceans and atmosphere could resume driving rapid heating despite the volcano-induced drop in emissions.
insights.speaker: Ilan Kelman
insights.so_what: Volcanic cooling would be temporary relief, not a fix for climate change.
